### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 48e695966ad76eee523d8a1321a88317ee4acfa6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fb61d66797998727d51c33a37b81fabd6d6d6c58` — the merge of head `f5b947e183d893b862280f9b677ee8b1187012a6` into base `48e695966ad76eee523d8a1321a88317ee4acfa6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fb61d66797998727d51c33a37b81fabd6d6d6c58 && git checkout fb61d66797998727d51c33a37b81fabd6d6d6c58
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 48e695966ad76eee523d8a1321a88317ee4acfa6 f5b947e183d893b862280f9b677ee8b1187012a6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 48e695966ad76eee523d8a1321a88317ee4acfa6 && git merge --no-ff f5b947e183d893b862280f9b677ee8b1187012a6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 48e695966ad76eee523d8a1321a88317ee4acfa6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 48e695966ad76eee523d8a1321a88317ee4acfa6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7abcd20e6b3e7a683143dc9804ee0974d95131b5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts,packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts,packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/field.json, ui/packages/fields/src/currency.ts, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/SummaryField.tsx, ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx, content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx

Inputs read: card #33659 (body, comments 6889945413, 6890000941, 6890800748), PR #33710 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), the check-runs on this head, ADR-0144 (D4, D5, D6 with its 2026-11-09 amendment, D8 rule 5). Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed. The tests, the regenerated reference pages and the changeset body are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Findings: one should-fix (S1), seven nits (N1 to N7), no must-fix.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ObjectSchema` accept set (object door, `refuseUnadmittedSummaryCurrency`): widened. A `sum` / `min` / `max` / `avg` summary with `currencyMode: 'dynamic'` (or a `currencyConfig` naming no mode), a `summaryOperations` naming a child object and field, and no `defaultCurrency` now parses. Right, and it is the only change: the `count` arm runs first and is untouched, a `dynamic` summary naming no child field or carrying a `defaultCurrency` is still refused, the `record` and `fixed` arms are unchanged. Nothing accepted before is refused now.
- `defineStack` accept set (`collectRecordCurrencyPathErrors`, new case (d)): of the roll-ups the object door now lets through, the stack admits only the one whose child field some `currencyConfig.homeAmount.field` on the child object names, when the stack declares the child and holds the field. Right. It is a strict subset of the object door's new set, so the stack door is narrower than the object door by design.
- The two doors therefore publish different accept sets, and the one a single-object save meets is the wider one. Wrong as left: see S1 under ③.
- `FieldSchema` and `CurrencyConfigSchema` accept sets: unchanged (text only in `field.zod.ts`). Right.
- No key, enum value, export or type is added or removed; `currencyMode` keeps its three values. Right.
- Console public surface: `summaryDeclaresCurrency` keeps its signature and now answers true for `dynamic` and for a config object with no mode; it answers false for a null or non-object config, as before. Right, and it is the one function both roll-up faces read.
- Liveness ledger row `field/currencyConfig`: a dated `WIDENED` line is prepended, the verdict stays LIVE, the evidence line is unchanged. Right: the reader it names is in this diff.
- Gate verdicts on this head: completed and green are Check Changeset (both runs), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Check Documentation Links, Type Check · source gates, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate and the planners. Still in progress or queued when read: Build Core, Build Docs, all eight Test Core shards, all sixteen Test UI shards, Type Check · workspace, · consumer gates, · debt ledger, Type Check UI, Lint UI, the Lint farm, Live E2E UI, Build & E2E UI. Those are not a pass. This record judges the contract; it does not stand in for them, and the landing condition (every check green) is unmet until they complete.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: a published accept set grows and nothing narrows. The changeset's sentence names which door refuses what, and it is accurate door by door.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` is right: a newly accepted value on an existing key, for one field type. No key is removed, no meaning or default changes (an absent `currencyConfig` on a summary still means no currency).
- `@objectstack/spec` `minor` matches the kind. `@object-ui/fields` `patch` is right for a renderer that starts honouring a declaration the spec newly admits; it publishes no new authorable surface. Both declaration lines are in the PR body and the changeset body, and `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` is a valid form of the third line; the seat owes the card and the rewrite to its number before ACCEPT.

### ③ Boundary flags

The report's `open_questions` is empty. Its three out-of-scope findings:

- (a) Single-object save admits a `dynamic` summary over a non-home child field. **S1, should-fix.** Read in the tree: a save or publish through the metadata API parses `ObjectSchema` and then asks `packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts#recordCurrencyFollowRefusal`, which judges only `record` roll-ups (`declaresRecordCurrency`) and record-mode child amounts. Before this PR that door refused every `dynamic` summary; after it, a `dynamic` summary over a `fixed` EUR amount, a plain number or a formula is stored and both faces draw it with the home currency's symbol. A roll-up over a record-mode amount is still refused there by D6's own door, whatever it declares. Judgment: this does not make the widening dishonest, for four reasons read off the tree. The changeset and the PR body state exactly which door judges home-ness. The staging has a precedent the ADR itself records (#31910 widened the spec ahead of #31911's engine door, with the child card filed). The Studio field form offers `currencyConfig` only on a `currency` field and a currency formula (`field.form.ts`), so the door is reached by a hand-written body, not by a click. And the declaration needed to reach it is one the author must write against the stated rule. But it is a real loss of refusal at a door users reach, and two things are missing: the follow-up has no carrier (`carrier: none`), and `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx` hides the gap. Its new bullet sits directly under the `record` bullet that promises `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 at the metadata API and says nothing of the running server, and its new paragraph says "`dynamic` is refused on any other roll-up" with no door. Owed before ACCEPT: file the `domain:server` card (a `dynamic` arm beside (c) in `recordCurrencyFollowRefusal`, sharing (d)'s wording the way (c) shares `record-currency-path.ts`), name it in the PR body in place of "not done here", and make the two `currency.mdx` sentences say that `defineStack` refuses it and a single-object save on a running server does not yet. That fix is prose plus a card; it moves no schema file.
- (b) Skills-docs follow-up on `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md`: acceptable. `skills/**` is outside the claim's surface, the line is in the PR body and the changeset, and the seat files the card.
- (c) Grid footer left to #33542: acceptable. The card's Ask names the footer, its Acceptance 1 to 3 do not, and the other lane holds `useColumnSummary.ts`. `Fixes #33659` will close the card with the footer unchecked, so the seat should leave the after-both-merge check on #33542 in writing rather than only in this PR's notes.

The PR's author is the fleet bot, so no relay note applies.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`.** Holds. The door can see only one object, so it lets through exactly the shape that could be the admitted roll-up (child object and field named, no code) and leaves home-ness to the pass that holds the child. Refusing a `defaultCurrency` here is right against D8 rule 5 ("Metadata never names the home currency") and against the reader, which ignores it under `dynamic`. The docblock's account of the arms matches the code. The refusal messages name the third admitted case and a remedy each.

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`.** Holds against ADR-0144. The test for "stored home amount" is the `homeAmount.field` pointer, the ADR's own definition (D5), and the object door `refuseDishonestHomeAmount` already guarantees that such a field is a stored `currency` field in `dynamic` mode, `readonly`, with no `expression`, claimed by one amount. So every row of it is in `localization.currency`, and D4's lock keeps the stored rows and the setting in step. The total is therefore in that currency for `sum`, `min`, `max` and `avg` alike, through any relation (a lookup included, since no row carries another currency). Tried against it:
  - home field renamed while the summary still names the old field: the child no longer holds the field, so (d) says nothing, as (c) says nothing. The roll-up itself is broken and is the engine's to report. **N4, nit**, accepted.
  - a roll-up of a parent's own `dynamic` home total (a nested summary), or of a plain `dynamic` currency field: refused, though both are drawn in the tenant currency in their own cells. This is the narrow reading the card's Acceptance 2 asks for. **N3, nit**; a follow-up if a consumer needs the nested total.
  - a home amount declared by an `objectExtensions` entry on a declared child: merged into the child's field map, so admitted. Right.
  - a summary on a parent the stack knows only through an extension, or a child it knows only that way: neither door judges it. This predates the PR for every mode, but `dynamic` now has a reader there. Likewise `homeAmountSourceOf` takes any field's `homeAmount.field` at its word, which the object door guarantees only for authored objects. **N6, N7, nits**; both belong in S1's server card.
  - `count`: never reaches (d); the object door refuses it in every mode.
  - (d) runs before (b), so a `dynamic` roll-up over a child amount that follows this record now gets (d)'s general prescription instead of (b)'s exact `currencyField` spelling, and (b)'s "It declares `currencyMode: 'dynamic'`" branch is reachable only for an extension-only child. The finding is still correct and reported once. **N2, nit.**
  - tenant with no home currency: `resolveFieldCurrency` answers nothing and the faces draw a plain amount; the spec side is unaffected.
  - summaries stored before the 2026-11-09 narrowing with a `dynamic` config now draw as money in the tenant currency. That is what the declaration said then; not measured whether any exists. **N5, nit**, accepted deviation.

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`.** The `CurrencyConfigSchema` docblock is accurate and names both doors. The `.describe()` on `FieldSchema.currencyConfig` says "any other `dynamic` summary ... are refused" without naming a door, the form the `record` clause beside it has always had; with S1 open it is true at `defineStack` only. **N1, nit**; leave the schema file alone and correct it with the server card.

**`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`.** Agrees with the tree sentence by sentence: the reader, the two faces, the two doors and "service-analytics is unchanged" all check out (`sourceFieldMeta` relays a code only under `fixed` and a pointer only under `record`, so `assertMeasureCurrenciesCoherent` has nothing to compare for a `dynamic` summary, as for the home field itself).

**`ui/packages/fields/src/currency.ts`, `widgets/SummaryField.tsx`, `index.tsx`.** Agree with the contract. `summaryDeclaresCurrency` reads an absent mode as `dynamic`, the spec's own parse. Both faces already pass the tenant currency and the parent row to `resolveFieldCurrency`, which answers the tenant default for a config that is neither `record` nor `fixed`: the call the metric tile makes for the home field. That meets the first consumer (record page, list cell) and Acceptance 3's "same currency as the tile". An undeclared summary is untouched (Acceptance 2). The comments describe the code.

**`content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx`, `field-types.mdx`.** Agree with the contract except the two sentences named in S1. The example is the admitted shape, and the page claims the record page and list cell only, not the footer.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review — delta

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4171fcd63b18043361dcb961844a216d439e3a2b`
Delta-of: 6890873219 (head `7abcd20e6b3e7a683143dc9804ee0974d95131b5`)
Local-runs: none
Scope: the net diff 7abcd20e..4171fcd6 and the PR body

Findings: no must-fix, no should-fix, one nit (D1). S1 is discharged.

### What the delta changes

Two commits (`396b6cfc`, `4171fcd6`), three files, 12 insertions and 7 deletions. The PR's head on GitHub is `4171fcd63b18043361dcb961844a216d439e3a2b`.

- `.changeset/33659-home-rollup-dynamic-currency.md`: one line. `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` becomes `Skills-docs: follow-up #33714`; the rest of the line is unchanged.
- `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx`: two passages. The `dynamic` bullet in "Roll-ups and datasets" (lines 257 to 266) and the closing paragraph of "Totals in the home currency" (lines 475 to 478).
- `ui/packages/fields/src/__tests__/summaryFaces.homeRollup-33659.test.tsx`: one line. The regex in the `text` helper held a literal non-breaking space (bytes `c2 a0`, read from the old blob with `od`); it is now `/ /g`. Both spell the same single code point U+00A0 with the same `g` flag and the same replacement, so the helper matches exactly what it matched before. No other line of the file moved, and no assertion changed.

No file under `packages/` is in the diff (`git diff --stat 7abcd20e 4171fcd6 -- packages` is empty). No schema, generated reference, liveness ledger or runtime source moved; the only code file is the test above.

### S1 discharge

- **(i) A `domain:server` card for the missing `dynamic` arm: done.** #33713 is open, labelled `finding` and `pm:blocked`, `Blocked-by: #33710`. Its body states the defect as the round-1 record did, and its fix shape is the one asked for: a `dynamic` arm in `recordCurrencyFollowRefusal` beside the `record` case, sharing case (d)'s wording. It also carries N1, N6 and N7. It suggests the lane `domain:server` in its text; the label itself is left to triage, which the card says.
- **(ii) The PR body names the card in place of "not done here": done.** The phrase "not done here" no longer appears in the body. The "Single-object saves" acceptance note now ends "Carrier: #33713", and the "Docs" line of the reader summary says both `currency.mdx` passages name `defineStack` as the refusing door and the single-object save as not judging it yet (#33713). The body's header lines agree with the changeset: `Clause-②: yes (widening ...)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Skills-docs: follow-up #33714`.
- **(iii) The two `currency.mdx` sentences: done, and true against the tree.**
  - The bullet now reads: `defineStack` (`os validate` and the build) refuses a `dynamic` summary over any other child field; a single-object save or publish through the metadata API on a running server does not judge the child field yet, because it parses the one object (#33713); the object itself refuses one naming no child field, one carrying a `defaultCurrency`, and a `count` in every mode, at every door.
  - The paragraph now reads: `defineStack` (`os validate` and the build) refuses `dynamic` on any other roll-up; a single-object save on a running server does not check that yet (#33713).
  - Checked at the new head. `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` case (d) (lines 4859 to 4867) pushes `dynamicRollupNotHomeError` when `homeAmountSourceOf(child, ops.field)` is undefined, so `defineStack` refuses it. `packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts#recordCurrencyFollowRefusal` (lines 521 to 594) skips every roll-up that does not satisfy `declaresRecordCurrency` (`currencyMode === 'record'`), in both the incoming-parent loop and the registered-other-end loop; it has no `dynamic` arm, so a single save does not judge it. `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts#refuseUnadmittedSummaryCurrency` (lines 2282 to 2297) refuses a `count` in any mode and a `dynamic` summary unless it names a child object and field and carries no `defaultCurrency`; it runs inside `ObjectSchema`, which every door parses, so "at every door" holds. `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` runs the `defineStack` refusals, matching the parenthesis.
  - A bare issue number in this docs folder is an existing convention (seven files under `content/docs/data-modeling/` carry one), and "Check Documentation Links" is green on the new head.

The skills follow-up is filed as #33714 (open, `documentation`, `finding`, `pm:blocked`) and both the changeset and the PR body name it.

### New findings

- **D1, nit.** The new bullet says a single-object save "refuses only what that object shows". One case is wider than that sentence: a `dynamic` summary over a record-mode child amount is still refused when the object registers, by D6's own door, which reads the child. The first bullet of the same list says so ("is refused when the object registers", whatever the summary declares), so a reader of the section is not misled. The same sentence names the single save and publish only; a batch writer's rows ask the same `recordCurrencyFollowRefusal` and so share the gap, which #33713's fix shape closes for every caller. No change owed in this PR; the sentence is rewritten anyway when #33713 lands.

Changeset: still well-formed. Front matter unchanged (`@objectstack/spec` minor, `@object-ui/fields` patch). The `Clause-②:` and `Metadata-protocol:` lines are byte-identical to the reviewed head; the `Skills-docs:` line now names a filed card instead of "owed". "Check Changeset" has one completed run green on the new head.

Checks on the new head when read: PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness and Governed Surface Queue Guard green; the lint, type-check, build and test jobs still in progress. This review ran nothing locally, so the Lint UI fix (the `no-irregular-whitespace` error) is confirmed by reading the bytes, not by a green ESLint job.

### Verdict

PASS. The delta is exactly the three prose and card items S1 asked for, plus a meaning-preserving escape in one test regex. Every owed item is done and the new prose agrees with the stack door, the object door and the engine door as they stand at `4171fcd6`. No schema or runtime file moved, the changeset is well-formed, and the one new finding is a nit carried by #33713.
